A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Many-for-Many (MfM) work and are readable throughout, including their appendices. The removed horse-comparison figure and subsequent figure renumbering can be identified reliably; there are no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original MfM benchmark evaluations, multi-task training ablations, generated examples, and an I2V user study in Tables 4–8 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablation results, user study, and most qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same conditional adapter, depth inputs, 3D-attention transformer, rectified-flow objective, and progressive joint image-video multi-task training. The 2B and 8B architectures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training-data coverage, VBench T2V/I2V evaluation, and the 16-task MfM benchmark remain unchanged. Although the horse illustration disappears, Appendix C still reports that scenario; the PDFs do not establish a removal from the underlying evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 4–6 and 8 retain their respective comparator sets, as do the retained qualitative comparisons. The horse comparison is removed as a whole, without selectively changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: The training recipe, evaluation metrics, and benchmark construction are unchanged. Both versions specify 480 MfM-benchmark samples, 50 diffusion steps, guidance scale 9.0, and a user study with 10 participants and 10 cases.

E4.justification: v2 removes the visual evidence for the horse I2V case study, which supported Appendix C's discussion of motion, anatomical fidelity, and scene interpretation. The multi-task ablation in Table 7 and Appendix F, other case comparisons, and Appendix G's failure analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates, rankings, and aggregated user-vote percentages. Neither adds or revises seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The generated horse sequences shown in v1 Figure 13 are absent from v2, removing qualitative result entries. All quantitative results in Tables 4–8 are unchanged, including MfM's reported average ranks of 3.04 for T2V and 3.33 for I2V; the horse-specific textual findings also remain.

T1.justification: The adapter dimensional relationships, positional-encoding construction, rectified-flow interpolation, and training objective in Section 3 and Equations 1–2 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified multi-task generation, reduced training-data requirements, improved video generation through joint learning, and competitive performance. The abstract's revision concerns model access information.

C2.justification: Interpretations of cross-task transfer, model behavior, and comparative performance remain unchanged, as do the multimodal-fusion limitation and documented failure conditions. Appendix C retains its horse-specific interpretations despite losing the corresponding figure.

D1.justification: v1 directs readers to one GitHub repository for models and code. v2 adds separate Hugging Face links labeled MfM-Pipeline-8B and MfM-Pipeline-2B while retaining the code link. This improves access instructions; the PDFs do not establish a change in actual resource availability. Implementation details are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The 65 references and related-work discussion are unchanged, including positioning against specialized video models and VACE. Text crossing different page boundaries does not alter the cited work or research positioning.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to the abstract's resource-availability sentence, figure cross-references, and version/date text. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact, with minor text reflow.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 13, showing horses running in dirt, is removed. v1 Figures 14–19 become v2 Figures 13–18 with their visual content preserved. Other figures and table displays are unchanged, apart from minor surrounding layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The direct model links improve access instructions, but v1 already pointed readers to models and code. Removing the horse comparison while retaining Appendix C's four-case description and horse-specific findings reduces the supporting evidence within the paper and creates an internal mismatch. With the method and quantitative evidence unchanged, this constitutes a limited net decline.
